newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 17 dead in India gelatine warehouse blast.
newsitem.headline: At least 17 dead in India gelatine warehouse blast.

text.p: At least 17 people died and 31 were injured on Thursday in two blasts at an explosives warehouse in the western state of Maharashtra, police said.

"We have recovered 17 bodies," Deputy Superintendent of Police Vijay Chavan told Reuters by telephone from the town of Satara in western Maharashtra. He said earlier reports by local news agencies that 38 people had died were incorrect.
"The death toll may go up by one or two when we clear the debris," Chavan said.
He said explosives experts were on their way to the site. Asked if he thought the explosions were caused by sabotage, Chavan said: "Absolutely not." He said the blasts were "absolutely an accident".
Chavan said the explosions occurred when gelatine was being unloaded from a sealed trailer towed by a van at the rear of the warehouse in Satara's Sangam Nagar suburb.
"There was first a small muffled explosion followed by a second big blast," Chavan said. He described the gelatine as "minor explosives" licensed for use in mining and construction.
He said most of the casualties were among people living in the neighbourhood and between 30 and 40 houses had been damaged by the blasts.
The dead included two children, three men and seven women, Chavan said. Five bodies were unidentified, he added.
The injured were taken to Satara Civil Hospital, he said.
Earlier, the United News of India (UNI) news agency said 38 people had died in the blast at the explosives warehouse.
Chavan said the explosions destroyed half the warehouse and flying debris killed a man driving a car on a nearby street.
The force of the blast hurled the engine of the explosives van through the walls of a house 700 yards (metres) away, he said.
